title: delivery-capability-manifest.v1
description: What delivery surfaces this SERVER supports, at which contract versions, bound to the exact schemas each surface speaks. The Delivery row of 02-contracts-and-data.md section 4 requires a 'capability manifest' and does not describe one; this is the drafted shape, and every field below is justified from a canon sentence rather than from convenience. WHY A SCHEMA AND NOT A MARKDOWN TABLE. Three reasons, in order of weight. (1) Section 4's rule is 'No Python-only type is treated as a public contract', and every other member of the Delivery row is a schema; a capability list that is prose is a public contract with no fixture and no validator, which is the exact gap Slice 3 exists to close. (2) Section 10 makes 'Contract mismatch -> status=unavailable, action=noop, expected and received versions recorded' a RUNTIME decision. A client can only make it by reading a machine-readable version declaration before its first call; prose cannot be read at handshake time, and hardcoding the versions in the client turns a detectable mismatch into a silent one. (3) It is the client-facing twin of app/api/contract_bindings.py: the same method/path-to-contract binding idea, published outward. Keeping them the same shape is what lets a conformance test compare what the server binds internally against what it advertises. WHAT IT IS NOT. It is not a run's delivery configuration - that is client-delivery-descriptor.v1.delivery, which is a per-run subset of what this manifest offers. The distinction has teeth: 03 section 4's 'direct_api is mutually exclusive with agent-facing modes' constrains a RUN, so the descriptor enforces it and this manifest deliberately does not. A server that supports all three modes and offers each to different runs is correct; a run that uses direct_api and hook_push together is not. Set semantics (at most one capability per kind) still apply, because two hook_push entries would leave 'which endpoint does hook_push use' ambiguous. BLINDING. This document is served to delivery clients, so it is under the same rule as the descriptor: no architecture, source, reader, storage or arm-label field, and additionalProperties false at every level so adding one fails validation rather than shipping. Nothing here varies by arm - two runs on different architectures see byte-identical capability manifests, which is what makes it safe to cache and to publish once.

contract_name.description: A contract name as app/contracts/registry.py resolves it: the schema file's basename with .schema.json removed, for example hook-request.experimental-v2. The pattern is the naming convention, not a guarantee the schema exists - resolution is the conformance suite's job and a name that resolves to nothing is a test failure there, not a validation failure here.

manifest_version.description: Version of this manifest document's own shape, distinct from the per-capability contract versions below. A client that cannot parse this number cannot trust anything after it.

descriptor_contract.description: The contract a client-delivery-descriptor fetch returns, so a client knows what GET /v1/experiment/runs/{run_id} will speak before it calls it (02 section 5).

contract.description: The experiment API major version, matching the /v1/ path prefix of 02 section 5.

oneOf.description: The pre-CLI mode (03 section 4.1). It binds no delivery schema of its own: a direct_api caller uses the experiment endpoints, whose bindings are app/api/contract_bindings.py, and it holds an experiment token to do so.

contract.description: The shared hook contract version. 2 is what 02 section 6 specifies and what hook-request/response.experimental-v2 carry in their own contract field, so a client can compare this number against the one it is about to send.

endpoint.description: Server-relative path, for example /v1/hook. Relative by construction, for the same reason as on the descriptor: an absolute URL in a server-published document is a redirect vector for a client's prompts.

triggers.description: Every trigger this server accepts. A run's descriptor advertises a SUBSET of these; the manifest is the ceiling, the descriptor is the selection.

request_contract.description: Pinned, not free. A manifest that could claim hook_push speaks some other request schema would let a server advertise a contract it does not implement, which is the one failure this document exists to prevent. A hook contract v3 changes contract, request_contract and response_contract together, in one visible diff.

tool.description: 02 section 7: 'The initial MCP surface contains one read-only tool.' Single-member closed enum, same discipline as error.v1's reason catalog. The optional collective_intelligence_explain(item_id) tool 'may be added after provenance retrieval is stable' - adding it is a schema-version change here, so a server cannot start advertising an unbuilt tool by editing a config value.

oneOf.description: The voluntary pull surface. 02 section 7: 'The tool is voluntary pull. It does not intercept another tool call' - which is why this capability declares an input and an output contract and no interception hook of any kind.

capabilities.description: What this server offers. The kinds are canon's delivery mode set (03 section 4: direct_api | hook_push | mcp_pull).

client_safety_ms.description: The safety ceiling this server expects clients to apply (03 section 4 runtime.client_safety_ms, 60000 in the pinned manifest). Published so a client sets its ceiling from the server's expectation instead of from a constant in its own source.

server_deadline_ms.description: The server's own deadline (03 section 4 runtime.server_deadline_ms, 55000 in the pinned manifest). Already client-visible on every hook response's deadline object, so publishing it here reveals nothing new and lets a client detect a nonsensical pair before the first call. NOT EXPRESSIBLE IN JSON SCHEMA, adapter-enforced: that server_deadline_ms is less than client_safety_ms - a cross-field comparison, and the relation 04 section 6 calls the 55/60-second safety limits.

published_at.description: When this manifest was published. Unlike client-delivery-descriptor.v1 this document carries no expiry: it describes the server build, not a run, and it stops being true when the server is redeployed rather than at a scheduled time.

allOf.description: At most one direct_api capability. minContains 0 makes it a cap rather than a requirement.
At most one hook_push capability. Two would leave the endpoint and trigger set ambiguous.
